model.title: READ Act
model.meta: Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions Committee · Sen. Bill Cassidy (R-LA)

summary.text: The bill would update federal rules for school reading programs by funding states to improve reading and writing instruction from early childhood through grade 12, with priority for states that are low-performing or serve many low-income families. It would define key terms such as the science of reading, high-impact tutoring, and universal early literacy screening, and would exclude certain three-cueing word-recognition methods from comprehensive literacy instruction. It would require states to screen students for reading difficulties, notify parents of students at risk, set aside grant funds by grade level, review teacher preparation programs for alignment with the science of reading, and publicly report results. It would also direct federal education researchers to study literacy and related topics such as screen time, and require the release of state-by-state National Assessment of Educational Progress reports to states.
